p1_fence.was: `if not fence['fenced']` accepted the truthy STRING 'false', and neither cause nor phase was checked at all -- so a stored cause of 'pass' or phase of 'queued' reached the remote discharge
p1_fence.now: `fence['fenced'] is not True` refuses any truthy non-boolean, and cause and phase are required to be 'cancelled' and 'block' beside the assignment and gate bindings that were already there
p1_fence.authority_for_those_values: not invented here. `authority/core.py`'s route_fenced compares a committed cancellation against exactly {'cause': 'cancelled', 'assignment': expect, 'phase': 'block', 'gate': gate, 'fenced': True}, so all five members are that owner's own semantics
p1_fence.historical_reads_preserved: every comparison is against the receipt's OWN assignment and the gate it composes; nothing reads the Work's current phase or gate, and a control proves a valid read still answers after the Work advances

p1_cleanup.was: the ending, the observed state and the operation pair were checked; kept, directory_custody and a foreign `kind` were not, so custody=None, an invented kept artifact or an extra member each returned positive proof and drove one real satisfy_gate
p1_cleanup.why_the_signature_could_not_catch_it: the recorded kind and operand signature are unchanged in those probes. Validating the REQUEST signature does not validate every member of the OUTCOME -- the review's own sentence, and the thing I had missed
now: the member set is exactly CLEANUP_RECEIPT with no optional: documents.cleanup_settled has no optional member and _settle_recordless_cleanup writes no `kind` on this family's endings, so admitting one was borrowing a sibling's allowance
kept must be exactly [] -- this family's own fact, not the ordinary reader's retention comparison: an abandonment intakes nothing and decides no retention
both normalization receipts are compared against custody.historical_directory_custody, the normalization owner's own read, so this module holds no second copy of that protocol
p1_cleanup.not_done: the ordinary cleanup family is not widened and no other owner's protocol is copied

p1_comments.was: two comments said a failed removal never journals
p1_comments.now: corrected in both places, naming that my own measured case in the same claim already established otherwise

p2_replay.was: after a discharge under policy 7, the same act under policy 9 returned the policy-7 receipt unrefused. The discharge identity is derived over the attempt and its fixed assignment alone -- deliberately, so a resuming manager re-derives it without the evidence -- which means the policy is not in it, and the receipt-signature check recomposes the receipt's own members, which were all consistent
p2_replay.now: the supplied policy is compared against the committed receipt and a difference is refused/operation-collision, as CONTRACT.md requires changed operands to do
p2_replay.no_mutable_read: compared against the receipt alone -- not today's cleanup row and not the Work -- so the lost-receipt retry and the later-generation replay both still work, each with its own control

each_negative_also_proves: no remote act and no local discharge receipt follow the refusal, which is the half the probes were actually about: the finding was one real satisfy_gate call behind bad evidence
